free_tier.stated: Serverless microVM sandboxes that the vendor says start in under 150 ms, scale to tens of thousands created concurrently and to millions of vCPUs, support stateful long-running sandboxes, ship preconfigured templates, and bill at millisecond granularity with no charge while nothing is executing. Templates, large-scale image distribution, arbitrary specifications and MCP, API and SDK access are listed. No free tier is published.

chaining: A microVM that bills only while executing is the right shape for evaluation fan-out, where a thousand short sandboxes each live a few seconds; it is the wrong shape for a service that must stay up, because the published selling point is that idle costs nothing precisely by not being a persistent host.

evidence.proved: 'sandboxes can start within 150ms and can be created concurrently at a scale of tens of thousands'; 'up to millions of vCPUs'; 'millisecond-level billing with no charges when not executing'; each sandbox is a microVM; MCP, API and SDK access
a third-party comparison lists USD 0.0351 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.0081 per GiB-hour with no free tier, which is a claim about a third party and not a reading of BytePlus's own rate card
the billing overview page returns only its navigation shell with no rate table, so the vendor's own numbers could not be read

notes: Recorded as reported because the vendor page establishes the product and its mechanics but not a price, and the documentation is a client-rendered shell that the broker could not read past. Routes tried: the product solution page (read, product facts only), docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/faas/Billing_overview (navigation shell, no table), docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/faas/Overview_of_cloud_sandbox (same shell), and a broad search that returned only third-party comparison tables. What would settle it: an account, which would expose the console rate card. Identity is left null rather than guessed: BytePlus sells to enterprises, and whether a personal account can top up without a company was not established. This is the one provider in this lane where the door is more likely to be the finding than the price.
